cases.title: First lesson: asks what should snap before proposing; candidates as questions, at most three; real names

rubric.reason: Turn 1 opens with a single framing sentence and sets no focus, then asks a real question, "Is either one meant to snap instead, like a blink, an on/off, or a cut?", and leaves the choice to the learner.
Turn 1 names two candidates by layer and property (Blink Opacity, Cut Opacity) and asks whether either is meant to snap, without calling either fade a mistake or telling the learner to hold anything.
Mentor Practice 2, Blink Opacity (3 pairs, first at 1 s), Cut Opacity (1 pair at 3 s) and Seal (precomp) all match the key_types_snapshot result in Turn 1.
Before proposing any focus, the mentor briefly notes that Blink and Cut fade and then asks as a real question: "Is anything here meant to snap, like a blink, an on/off, or a cut?"

Only two candidates (Blink and Cut Opacity) are named, and they are put as a question ("Is either of those meant to switch on and off at once instead of fading?"), never called a mistake or an instruction to hold.
Mentor Practice 2, Blink Opacity at 1 s with three pairs, Cut Opacity at 3 s with one pair, and Seal as a precomp all match the key_types_snapshot result.
